text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Syrian newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Syrian-Lebanese coordination committee approves a number of agreements aimed at boosting bilateral cooperation during talks in Damascus. Syrian and Lebanese prime ministers ratify minutes of the meeting which reiterated commitment to the basis of a just and comprehensive peace.
- Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu repeats call for unconditional peace talks. Netanyahu ignores withdrawal from the Golan, U.N resolutions and the land for peace principle.
- Israel shells south Lebanon and the resistance destroys enemy vehicle.
- Israeli occupation forces arrest four Syrians in the Golan.
- Netanyahu's government approves establishment of 60 settlement units in the West Bank and plans another 200.

- Syrian Vice-President Abdel-Halim Khaddam receives Sudan's Vice-President al-Zubeir Mohammad Saleh. Says: "Syria stands by the unity of Sudan and rejects any foreign interference in its internal affairs."
- France says Europe wants a bigger role in the Middle East peace process.
- European envoy Miguel Angel Moratinos to start a visit to Damascus on Friday.
- Khaddam discusses situation in the region and bilateral ties during a meeting with Lebanese Prime Minister Hariri.
